\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بحث} \ur{کرنا} (bahas karnā)}{بحث کرنا (bahas karnā)}]{\ur{بحث} \ur{کرنا} (bahas karnā) — to argue; to debate}

\label{lesson:UR-C334-bahas-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a benefit, then the Urdu for to use.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بحث} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{بحث} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{bahas karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to argue; to debate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{دونوں} \ur{ہر} \ur{بات} \ur{پر} \ur{بحث} \ur{کرتے} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh donoṅ har bāt par bahas karte haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Those two argue about everything.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{استاد} \ur{سے} \ur{بحث} \ur{کی}, \emph{us ne ustād se bahas kī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بحث} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{bahas karnā}) is built from \emph{bahas}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{baḥth}, \textquotedblleft{}an inquiry, a discussion\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahas karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahas karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{voh donoṅ har bāt par bahas karte haiṅ.} — Those two argue about everything.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a benefit, then the Urdu for to use, then say \emph{bahas karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بحث} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To argue; to debate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\label{lesson:UR-C334-dalil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to use, then the Urdu for to argue.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دلیل}}
\textbf{\ur{دلیل}} — \emph{dalīl} — \textquotedblleft{}a reasoned argument; a plea\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{آپ} \ur{کی} \ur{دلیل} \ur{مضبوط} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹوکنا} (ṭoknā)}{ٹوکنا (ṭoknā)}]{\ur{ٹوکنا} (ṭoknā) — to interrupt; to cut in}

\label{lesson:UR-C334-tokna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to argue, then the Urdu for a reasoned argument.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹوکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹوکنا}} — \emph{ṭoknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to interrupt; to cut in\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میں} \ur{بات} \ur{کر} \ur{رہا} \ur{تھا} \ur{اور} \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مجھے} \ur{ٹوکا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṅ bāt kar rahā thā aur us ne mujhe ṭokā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I was speaking and he cut me off.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مجھے} \ur{ٹوکا}, \emph{us ne mujhe ṭokā}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تکرار} (takrār)}{تکرار (takrār)}]{\ur{تکرار} (takrār) — an altercation; a row}

\label{lesson:UR-C334-takrar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a reasoned argument, then the Urdu for to interrupt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تکرار}}
\textbf{\ur{تکرار}} — \emph{takrār} — \textquotedblleft{}an altercation; a row\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دکان} \ur{پر} \ur{گاہک} \ur{اور} \ur{دکاندار} \ur{میں} \ur{تکرار} \ur{ہوئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dukān par gāhak aur dukāndār meṅ takrār huī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A customer and the shopkeeper had a row in the shop.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تکرار}} (\emph{takrār}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{takrār}, \textquotedblleft{}repetition\textquotedblright{}; the sense \textquotedblleft{}a row\textquotedblright{}, words thrown back and forth, is Urdu's own, as far as our sources show.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{منطق} (mantiq)}{منطق (mantiq)}]{\ur{منطق} (mantiq) — logic}

\label{lesson:UR-C334-mantiq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to interrupt, then the Urdu for an altercation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{منطق}}
\textbf{\ur{منطق}} — \emph{mantiq} — \textquotedblleft{}logic\textquotedblright{}.
